jcr:content.jcr:title: Brean Down Coastal Walk
jcr:content.jcr:description: A climb onto a Somerset headland with sea views and a historic fort.
jcr:content.shortDescription: A climb onto a Somerset headland with sea views and a historic fort.

placeabout.heading: About this place
placeabout.description:
Brean Down is a substantial coastal adventure rather than a flat seafront stroll. The headland reaches into the Bristol Channel, and its fort and open landscape give older children a destination to work towards.

Plan from the National Trust trail guide, taking account of the climb and your family's walking experience. Our family idea: bring binoculars and use a sheltered stop to compare the coast on either side of the Down.

placepracticalinfo.heading: Practical information
placepracticalinfo.bestFor: Older children and experienced family walkers.
placepracticalinfo.facilities: Visitor facilities at the base of the Down; little shelter on the headland.
placepracticalinfo.parking: Use the signed Brean Down parking area and check current charges.
placepracticalinfo.goodToKnow: Expect steep steps or an uphill approach, exposed weather and dangerous cliffs. Keep children well back from edges and avoid tidal mud on the beach.

placevisitmap.heading: Plan your visit
placevisitmap.travelNote: Use the signed Brean Down parking area and check current charges. Use this postcode for the arrival area, then follow local signs to the entrance. Google Maps can use your current location, or you can enter a starting point.
